Figure 1: Distribution of positive transformed responses entering the two primary models. Exact-zero observations, which map to −1, are reported separately inside each panel. | Two histograms show the transformed positive melEDI observations for the near-eye and chest model frames on separately scaled vertical axes. Both distributions rise broadly between transformed values of zero and about 2.5 before declining. Panel annotations report that approximately one third of observations were exact zero and therefore mapped to minus one.

Figure 2: Clock-bin support in the primary near-eye and complementary chest model frames. | Two heatmaps show the percentage of fitted participant-days contributing an observation at each half-hour of local time for every site. Most cells have high coverage, with modest site- and time-specific gaps.

Figure 3: Number of supported 30-minute observations per fitted participant-day. | Two bar charts show that most fitted participant-days contributed 45 to 48 half-hour observations, while a smaller number contributed between 38 and 44 observations.

Figure 4: Recorded residual autocorrelation before and after the boundary-aware AR(1) correction. | Line charts for near-eye and chest fits show residual correlation across lags of 30 to 180 minutes. Correlation is high before AR correction and close to zero after correction.

Direct comparison of near-eye and chest patterns

Figure 1: Daily near-eye melEDI patterns: site-average curve (A), site curves (B), participant curves (C), and site-to-global-time-effect factors (D). Ribbons are pointwise 95% CIs. | Four-panel near-eye daily-pattern figure. Panel A shows the site-average global time effect for 816 participant-days with a pointwise 95% confidence ribbon. Panel B shows nine site curves, pointwise ribbons, country-coded site labels, and a participant-day count in each facet. Panel C shows participant curves. Panel D shows site-to-global-time-effect factors with pointwise ribbons; red segments mark individual clock times whose intervals exclude one.

Figure 2: Daily chest melEDI patterns: site-average curve (A), site curves (B), participant curves (C), and site-to-global-time-effect factors (D). Ribbons are pointwise 95% CIs. | Four-panel chest daily-pattern figure. Panel A shows the site-average global time effect for 902 participant-days with a pointwise 95% confidence ribbon. Panel B shows eight site curves, pointwise ribbons, country-coded site labels, and a participant-day count in each facet. Panel C shows participant curves. Panel D shows site-to-global-time-effect factors with pointwise ribbons; red segments mark individual clock times whose intervals exclude one.

Figure 3: Near-eye and chest site curves for the same 112 participants, 643 participant-days, and 29,786 30-minute observations at both sensor positions. Ribbons are component pointwise 95% CIs. | Eight country-coded site facets compare separately fitted near-eye and chest daily melEDI curves for the same 112 participants, 643 participant-days, and 29,786 half-hour observations at both sensor positions. Near-eye curves are solid blue and chest curves are dashed orange; translucent ribbons show component pointwise 95% confidence intervals.
